question: Does the shared-Gaussian reflection (2026-10-17_mirror_b_shared_dc) still work without the GT mirror normal? (user: the mirror image is much sharper but the mirror is not perfectly flat; try 1) plain StableNormal normals, 2) no normal prior on the mirror = nmask)
parent_experiment: 2026-10-17_mirror_b_shared_dc (envgs_b300_gtnorm_shared): same code, same shared_reflection: True, DC hit colour, one bounce
code: identical to 2026-10-17_mirror_b_shared_dc.patch (checked with cmp at launch); EnvGS HEAD 09993470ae76854e2dae1118374031c9b32891ac + that patch

stablenormal_shared.meaning: 1) plain StableNormal prior everywhere, mirror included (user correction at 15:00: 'the first one should use the StableNormal normals directly')

changes_vs_gtnorm_shared.data_root: b300 instead of b300_gtnorm (StableNormal on mirror pixels instead of GT plane normal)

changes_vs_envgs_b300.sampler_cfg.shared_reflection: true (only line that differs in the resolved config)

nmask_shared.meaning: 2) no normal prior on mirror pixels only (StableNormal elsewhere), same as envgs_b300_nmask
nmask_shared.data_root: data/datasets/mirror_b/b300_nmask (GT mirror pixels persp/masks == 3 stored black in normals/)

changes_vs_gtnorm_shared.supervisor_cfg.norm_ignore_zero: true (black prior pixels skipped in the normal loss)

resolved_config_diff_check: diff vs envgs_b300_gtnorm_shared resolved config (after renaming exp_name) shows only the data_root / preload paths and the one supervisor line listed above
common_settings: 60000 iters (120 x 500), perc_loss_start_iter 45000, render_reflection_start_iter 3000, val = every 8th frame (38 views), GT poses, conda env envgs (torch 2.3.1+cu118)
evaluation_plan: eval_mirror_b_run.sh <tag> dataset_b300 <gpu>; tools/per_obj_mirror_b.py; frame 88 crop vs GT; additionally mirror flatness: spread of rendered mirror depth around the GT plane (user noted the mirror is not perfectly flat)

results.eval: eval_mirror_b_run.sh <run> dataset_b300 1; per_obj_mirror_b.py; mirror_flatness_b.py (signed depth err on eroded GT mirror px); mirror_normal_spread_b.py (angle to per-frame median rendered normal on mirror px)

nmask_shared.summary: Failed: without a normal prior on the mirror, shared reflection switches off (specular weight 0.06) and the mirror is painted as a texture with geometry pulled ~8 cm in front of the plane and wavy (normal spread 11 deg). Mirror PSNR 21.45, worst of all runs; opaque PSNR highest (41.0).

stablenormal_shared.summary: Shared reflection with the plain StableNormal prior: most of the mirror is a clean plane (normal spread median 0.4 deg) but ~17% of mirror pixels have normals ~90 deg off (where StableNormal sees the reflected floor/ceiling/side walls), so plane fraction drops 0.919 -> 0.838 vs the env-GS baseline. Mirror PSNR 25.94 -> 26.47, specular weight 0.25 -> 0.54, LPIPS 0.0778. Far below gtnorm_shared (28.83, plane 0.999).

results.conclusion: With one shared set of Gaussians the mirror normal prior matters more than with env Gaussians: GT normal -> best of all runs (mirror 28.83); StableNormal -> 26.47 with ~17% of the mirror tilted to the wrong (reflected-surface) normal; no prior on the mirror -> collapse (reflection switched off, mirror painted as texture, 21.45). Motivates a geometry cue independent of the reflected content (LiDAR mirror-surface echoes).

nonorm_shared.meaning: 1) no monocular normal prior at all
nonorm_shared.data_root: data/datasets/mirror_b/b300 (StableNormal normals still loaded by the dataset, not used by any loss)
